【Analytical Framework and Study Aim · s1-4-p1】Drawing these strands together, the study used 4 sensitizing domains: role clarity, interaction affordance, social mediation, and organizational embedding. Role clarity concerns whether the robot has an obvious and locally meaningful purpose. Interaction affordance concerns whether visitors and staff can understand how to start, continue, benefit from, and recover from interaction. Social mediation concerns whether signage, demonstration, and visible endorsement reduce uncertainty and invite use. Organizational embedding concerns workflow, training, support, maintenance, content management, and responsibility. The 4 domains were developed as an author synthesis of TAM, UTAUT, the Almere model, and implementation evidence [10,11,16-20]. They guided deductive coding and mixed methods interpretation, while inductive analysis remained open to recurrent issues raised by staff. The framework is provisional and is not presented as a validated scale.

【Acceptance and Implementation of Health Care Robots · s1-3-2-p3】Acceptance models alone do not capture implementation fully. Reviews of SARs in health and social care identify insufficient training, unclear role boundaries, additional workload, technical unreliability, privacy and safety concerns, weak customization, and the absence of local champions or maintenance structures as recurring barriers [10,11,19]. Stakeholder-oriented design studies similarly indicate that acceptability improves when robot functions are visibly useful, easy to understand, robust in busy environments, and aligned with actual care needs [11].

【Acceptance and Implementation of Health Care Robots · s1-3-2-p1】Technology acceptance research offers a useful starting point. The technology acceptance model (TAM) identifies perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use as central drivers of adoption [16]. The UTAUT (unified theory of acceptance and use of technology) adds social influence and facilitating conditions, which are particularly relevant when technologies are introduced through organizational channels [17]. Staff and visitors assess technical capability together with usefulness, understandability, approachability, and visible social endorsement.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Evaluating Human-Robot Interaction With a Socially Assistive Robot in Pediatric Health Care: Mixed Methods Pilot Study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Main Findings · s4-1-p1】This mixed methods pilot examined how a socially assistive robot was received in a pediatric outpatient setting and which conditions shaped practical acceptance. Across all 4 observed indicators (looking at the robot, approaching it, touching it, and using the robot’s screen or app), interaction was lowest when the robot was present without explanation, increased when a poster clarified its role, and was highest when an intern invited and demonstrated use. Staff accounts provided a complementary implementation perspective rather than a direct explanation of visitors’ experiences. Staff evaluated the robot as a service tool whose value depended on a concrete role, relevant and multilingual content, technical support, workflow fit, and visible organizational ownership.

【Main Findings · s4-1-p2】Taken together, observed visitor behavior and staff perceptions informed the provisional mediated acceptance framework. The robot’s hardware, location, and interface did not change across the 3 field phases; the surrounding support did. The results should nevertheless be read as descriptive associations. The sequential naturalistic design does not establish that the poster or facilitator alone caused the observed differences.

【Acceptance and Implementation of Health Care Robots · s1-3-2-p2】For social robots, the Almere model extends acceptance thinking by incorporating trust, enjoyment, social presence, and anxiety [18]. Although developed in work with older adults, its broader insight is relevant here: acceptance of a social agent reflects both functional evaluation and the felt quality of interaction. In pediatric contexts, playful engagement, attention redirection, and perceived warmth may matter alongside instrumental usefulness [8,9].
